excerpt: Investment treaties, investor-state dispute settlement, and regulatory sovereignty explain how international economic law protects foreign investment while constraining, reshaping, and contesting public regulation. This article examines bilateral investment treaties, investment chapters, ICSID arbitration, UNCITRAL arbitration, consent, jurisdiction, protected investors, protected investments, fair and equitable treatment, expropriation, national treatment, most-favored-nation clauses, umbrella clauses, damages, enforcement, transparency, treaty shopping, counterclaims, and reform. It shows how investment law governs disputes over taxation, public health, environment, energy transition, infrastructure, land, privatization, financial regulation, and crisis measures. The article also addresses climate policy, human rights, development, democratic accountability, regulatory chill, and treaty modernization. By connecting doctrine, institutions, case studies, and lawyer-facing workflows, it shows how ISDS turns regulatory sovereignty into a central battleground of global economic law and contemporary international legal politics today.
